mainTopic: Selling an עובר, or an animal only for its fetuses, to a non-Jew according to רבי יהודה and the רבנן
overview: Background: חכמים forbade selling a large work animal to a non-Jew, because he will work it on שבת. רבי יהודה permits selling a שבורה, a broken animal that can never be healed. The גמרא first asks whether רבי יהודה also permits selling an עובר. A ברייתא about giving an animal בקבלה seems to forbid it, but that proof is pushed off: the ברייתא may be about the mother. רב אשי then proves from רבי יהודה's own reason that a fetus, which will one day work, is forbidden. A second version (איכא דמתני) places this discussion on our משנה and explains that a fetus is in its natural state, unlike a broken animal. Next the גמרא asks whether one may sell an animal to a גוי only for its fetuses, according to both רבי יהודה and the רבנן. Along the way it clarifies that the רבנן's reason is fear of confusion. It then tries to settle the question from the משנה's wording, but that proof is rejected. Finally it brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה calls giving an animal בקבלה 'not permitted', and the חכמים exempt any animal partly owned by a גוי from בכורה. The discussion of this proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Trying to read the ברייתא as talking about the fetus
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that the ברייתא's words 'he is not permitted' refer to selling the עובר. That would prove selling a fetus to a non-Jew is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't the ברייתא talking about the fetus?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has just quoted a ברייתא of רבי יהודה about a Jew who gives his animal to a non-Jew בקבלה, 'although he is not permitted'. It now suggests that this 'not permitted' refers to the fetus, which would prove that handing a fetus over to a non-Jew is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the seller is 'not permitted' and gets fined. If 'not permitted' refers to the עובר itself, then selling an unborn animal is forbidden, even though it cannot work right now.

phrases.english: What, is it not referring to the fetus?
phrases.notes: Refers to the ברייתא's statement that he is 'not permitted' to sell.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the intended inference from the ברייתא quoted on the previous amud.
steps.raayaObject: Selling an עובר to a non-Jew is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יהודה stating that one who gives an animal to a non-Jew in receivership (בקבלה), 'although he is not permitted', is fined and gives all its value to the כהן.

steps.title: No, it refers to the mother animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The 'not permitted' is about the בהמה, the mother, not the fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is referring to the animal itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof by giving the ברייתא a different reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the problem is handing over the full-grown mother, the ברייתא tells us nothing new about a fetus. So this ברייתא cannot settle the question about רבי יהודה and an עובר. רב אשי settles it in step 7.

phrases.english: No, it is referring to the animal.
phrases.notes: The forbidden part is selling the mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only this reading of the ברייתא, not the possibility that a fetus is forbidden.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's 'not permitted' can refer to the mother animal rather than the fetus.

steps.title: The word 'its value' is masculine
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says דמיו (masculine). That fits the עובר, not the בהמה, which is feminine.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא says 'its value' in the masculine form!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection by pointing to the grammar of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עובר is a masculine noun and בהמה is feminine. Since the ברייתא says דמיו with a masculine ending, it seems to be talking about the fetus after all.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches! (introduces a textual challenge)

phrases.english: But doesn't it teach 'its value' (masculine)!
phrases.notes: Masculine suffix points to the עובר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading proposed in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא refers to the mother animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The masculine word דמיו matches עובר, not the feminine בהמה.

steps.title: Change the wording to feminine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by changing the text to דמיה (feminine).
steps.simpleTranslation: Read it as 'its value' in the feminine form.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the grammar problem by changing one letter in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the feminine form, the fine is the value of the בהמה. This keeps the reading of step 2 alive.

keyTerms.meaning: Teach / read it this way (a text emendation)

steps.confusionAlert: תני here does not mean we found a different manuscript. The גמרא is adjusting the wording so the ברייתא fits the reading it wants to keep.

phrases.english: Teach: 'its value' (feminine).
phrases.notes: Emends the ברייתא to refer to the בהמה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the grammar challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The masculine wording proves the ברייתא is about the fetus.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording should be read as feminine, referring to the mother animal.

steps.title: Why would the כהן get the money for a mother animal?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the money goes to the כהן. That only makes sense for a בכור, which is the fetus, not the mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches: 'he gives all its value to the כהן.' If it is about the animal, what does the כהן have to do with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a stronger challenge that a simple word change cannot fix.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן receives a בכור, a firstborn. The mother is not a בכור. Since the fine goes to the כהן, the ברייתא must be talking about the firstborn עובר.

phrases.english: But doesn't it teach 'he gives all its value to the priest',
and if it is about the animal,
what does the priest have to do with it?
phrases.notes: Only a בכור goes to a כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, stronger attack on the reading defended in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the ברייתא refers to the mother animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Money given to a כהן only fits a בכור, which is the עובר.

steps.title: A pregnant animal given to a non-Jew to fatten
steps.stepSummary: The case is a Jew who gave a pregnant animal to a non-Jew to fatten. He is fined for the animal, and that fine is extended to the fetus, whose value goes to the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with a case where he gave him a pregnant animal to fatten. Since we fine him for the animal, we also fine him for the fetus.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the ברייתא's case so that the forbidden act is still about the mother, yet the כהן still gets paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Handing the mother over to the non-Jew is the forbidden act. Because חכמים already penalize him for that, they extend the penalty to the עובר, and he must pay its value as a בכור to the כהן. So the ברייתא does not prove that selling a fetus alone is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here? (redefines the case)
Since (one thing is true, another follows along)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא proof fails. Its case is about handing over the mother, and the fetus is only fined along with her (מיגו). So this ברייתא does not show that a fetus by itself is forbidden. רב אשי's proof in the next step settles that.

phrases.english: Here, with what are we dealing?

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן דְּיָהֵיב לֵיהּ בְּהֵמָה מְעַבַּרְתָּא לְפַטּוֹמַהּ,
phrases.english: Such as where he gave him a pregnant animal to fatten,
phrases.notes: A Jew gives the animal to a non-Jew in a profit-sharing deal.

phrases.english: so since we penalize him for the animal,
we penalize him for the fetus.
phrases.notes: Hence the payment to the כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by redefining the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Payment to the כהן proves the forbidden act was selling the fetus.
steps.terutzMaskana: The forbidden act is handing over the mother, and the fetus is fined along with her.

steps.title: רב אשי proves it from רבי יהודה's own reason
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה permits a שבורה only because it can never be healed. So an animal that can 'heal' stays forbidden, and a fetus will eventually be able to work, so it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Come and hear: רבי יהודה permits a broken animal because it cannot be healed. This implies that one that can be healed, he forbids. A fetus is also like one that can be healed. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings a new proof, this time from רבי יהודה's own reasoning, and concludes that selling a fetus is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key is the reason רבי יהודה gives: 'because it cannot be healed.' This shows the issue is not only whether the animal works now, but whether it will ever work. An עובר will grow and work, so it counts as 'able to heal', and it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it (the proof is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, what matters is whether the animal will ever be able to work. A fetus will, so selling it to a non-Jew is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a reason stated in a ruling can define its limits. The phrase 'because it cannot be healed' rules out the fetus.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Come and hear,
Rabbi Yehuda permits with a broken animal,
because it cannot be healed.
This implies that if it can be healed, he forbids,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא עוּבָּר נָמֵי כְּיָכוֹל לְהִתְרַפְּאוֹת דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: and a fetus too is like one that can be healed.
phrases.notes: It will be able to work in the future.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא proof failed, רב אשי offers a new and successful proof.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה forbids selling an עובר to a non-Jew.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's stated reason for permitting a שבורה: it cannot be healed.

steps.title: A second version: the discussion is on our משנה
steps.stepSummary: Some place this discussion on our משנה, which says one who sells a fetus to a non-Jew, 'although he is not permitted', is exempt from בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some teach it on our משנה: 'and one who sells to him, even though he is not permitted.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up an alternate version of the discussion by quoting the line from our משנה it will be attached to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the starting point is not a general question but our משנה itself. The משנה's phrase 'although he is not permitted' will now be tested against רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: And some teach it (an alternate version)

phrases.english: And there are those who teach it on our Mishnah,
'and one who sells to him,'
phrases.notes: Sells the fetus of his donkey to a non-Jew.

phrases.english: 'although he is not permitted.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a second version of the same discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה says selling a fetus to a non-Jew is 'not permitted'.

steps.title: Does our משנה disagree with רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יהודה permits a שבורה that cannot work, perhaps he also permits a fetus. If so, our משנה, which forbids it, would not follow him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say our משנה is not like רבי יהודה? For we learned: רבי יהודה permits a broken animal!
steps.whatsHappening: In the second version, the גמרא questions whether our משנה goes against רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עובר, like a שבורה, cannot work right now. If רבי יהודה permits anything that cannot work, he would permit selling a fetus, which contradicts our משנה's 'not permitted'. The next step answers this by distinguishing a damaged animal from a fetus in its natural state.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (suggests a troubling conclusion)
As we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: Shall we say our Mishnah is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda,
as we learned: Rabbi Yehuda permits with a broken animal!
phrases.notes: Quoted from עבודה זרה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the challenge on the משנה line quoted in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: Our משנה's ruling that selling a fetus to a non-Jew is 'not permitted'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה permits an animal that cannot work, and a fetus cannot work either, so the משנה would seem to disagree with him.

steps.title: Our משנה can follow רבי יהודה: a fetus is not like a broken animal
steps.stepSummary: Even רבי יהודה would forbid a fetus. A שבורה is in an abnormal, damaged state, but a fetus is in its normal state of growing.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say our משנה follows רבי יהודה. A broken animal is not in its normal state. A fetus is in its normal state.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 9. It shows that our משנה can still follow רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה permits selling a שבורה because it is damaged and out of the normal order. A fetus is not damaged; it is just at an early, natural stage and will grow into a working animal. So permitting a שבורה tells us nothing about a fetus.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (the answer can fit even this opinion)
A broken or damaged animal that cannot work
Its normal way or natural state

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabbi Yehuda —
a broken animal, that is not its normal state;
phrases.notes: It is damaged, which is abnormal.

phrases.english: a fetus, that is its normal state.
phrases.notes: Every animal starts as a fetus, so it is not 'damaged'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (abnormal damage vs. a natural stage of growth)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יהודה permits a non-working שבורה, he would also permit a non-working fetus.
steps.terutzMaskana: A fetus is in its natural state and will work later, so even רבי יהודה may forbid it.

steps.title: A ברייתא of רבי יהודה seems to forbid giving over a fetus
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה says that giving an animal to a גוי 'is not permitted' and carries a fine. It suggests this refers to the fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יהודה says, if a Jew receives an animal from a גוי to raise, and it gives birth, we value the calf, and he gives half its value to the כהן. And if a Jew gives his animal to a גוי to raise, even though he is not allowed to, we fine him up to ten times its value, and he gives all of its value to the כהן. Isn't this talking about the fetus?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove that רבי יהודה really does forbid giving a fetus to a גוי. If so, our משנה clearly matches him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'even though he is not permitted' and then sends the money to the כהן. Money for the כהן fits a בכור, which is the newborn. So the 'not permitted' seems to be about the fetus. This is the same ברייתא used in the first version; here it is used to support the answer in Step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a proof from a source)
One who takes in an animal to raise and share profits
We assess it at its value

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא has two cases. In the first, a Jew takes an animal from a גוי. In the second, a Jew gives his animal to a גוי. Only the second case is 'not permitted' and fined.

phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One who takes in an animal from a non-Jew to raise, and it gave birth —
we assess it at its value,
and he gives half its value to the Kohen.
phrases.notes: His half-share of the firstborn is holy as a בכור.

phrases.english: And one who gives the non-Jew an animal to raise,
even though he is not permitted —
we fine him up to ten times its value,
phrases.notes: He must buy back the non-Jew's share, even at a high price.

phrases.english: and he gives all of its value to the Kohen.
Isn't this about the fetus?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to back up Step 10 with a source showing רבי יהודה forbids a fetus.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה forbids giving or selling a fetus to a גוי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי יהודה that fines one who gives an animal to a גוי and sends all the value to the כהן.

steps.title: No, the ברייתא is about the mother animal
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. The 'not permitted' may refer to giving the mother animal itself, not the fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is about the animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. It reads the ברייתא as forbidding the mother animal, not the fetus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving a full-grown working animal to a גוי is clearly forbidden. So the ברייתא may only be talking about that, and it tells us nothing about a fetus.

phrases.english: No, it is about the animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the reading that the ברייתא is about the fetus.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The prohibition and fine can be explained as being about the mother animal.

steps.title: But the ברייתא says 'its value' in the masculine
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says דמיו, a masculine form. That fits the fetus (עובר, masculine), not the animal (בהמה, feminine).
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches 'his/its value' (masculine)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 12 from the grammar of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בהמה is a feminine word, so its value would be דמיה. The masculine דמיו points to the עובר.

phrases.english: But it teaches 'its value' in the masculine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the pushback of Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא is about the mother animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The masculine word דמיו fits עובר, not the feminine בהמה.

steps.title: Read the word as feminine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the text to דמיה, the feminine form, which refers to the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach 'her value'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing one letter in the ברייתא's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the reading דמיה, the word refers to the mother animal, and the grammar question disappears.

phrases.english: Teach 'her value'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word דמיו proves the ברייתא is about the fetus.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read דמיה; the ברייתא is about the mother animal.

steps.title: But why would the כהן get the money for the mother?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says all the value goes to the כהן. A כהן only gets a בכור, not the mother animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches, 'he gives all its value to the כהן.' If it is about the animal, what does the כהן have to do with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading that the ברייתא is about the mother animal again, this time from where the money goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing one word fixed the grammar, but the כהן still gets the money. The כהן has no share in the mother, only in the firstborn, so the ברייתא seems to be about the fetus after all.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the כהן have to do with it?

phrases.english: But it teaches, 'he gives all its value to the Kohen,'
and if it is about the animal —
what does the Kohen have to do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second attack on the reading of Step 12, which survived Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא's prohibition is about the mother animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Money goes to the כהן only for a בכור, which is the fetus.

steps.title: The case is a pregnant animal given over to be fattened
steps.stepSummary: The Jew gave a pregnant animal to the גוי. He is fined for the forbidden act with the mother, and the fine is extended to the fetus, whose value goes to the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with a case where he gave a pregnant animal to be fattened. Since we fine him for the animal, we also fine him for the fetus.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 15 by explaining the exact case of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition is only about the mother. Since he is already being fined for her, the חכמים extend the fine to the fetus too, and that money goes to the כהן. So the ברייתא still does not prove that a fetus alone is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
Since (one thing applies, so does the other)

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with here?
For example, where he gave a pregnant animal to be fattened,
since we fine him for the animal —
we also fine him for the fetus.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 15. This leaves the proof of Step 11 rejected.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן's share proves the prohibition is about the fetus.
steps.terutzMaskana: The prohibition is about the mother, and the fine is extended to the fetus.

steps.title: רב אשי proves רבי יהודה forbids a fetus
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה permits a שבורה only because it can never heal. A fetus is like an animal that can 'heal', since it will work later, so it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Come and hear. רבי יהודה permits a broken animal because it cannot be healed. This implies that if it can be healed, it is forbidden. A fetus is also like something that can be healed. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings a clear proof that settles the question. רבי יהודה forbids a fetus, so our משנה follows him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason רבי יהודה gives for permitting a שבורה is that it can never become a working animal. A fetus will become a working animal, so it does not fit that reason. This confirms the answer of Step 10.
steps.whatToRemember: Even רבי יהודה forbids selling a fetus of large livestock to a גוי. He permits only an animal that will never be able to work, and a fetus will work one day. So our משנה ('although he is not permitted') fits רבי יהודה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The test for רבי יהודה is whether the animal will ever be able to work. Being unable to work right now is not enough.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Come and hear:
Rabbi Yehuda permits a broken animal,
because it cannot be healed.
This implies that if it can be healed — it is forbidden,
and this fetus is also like one that can be healed.
phrases.notes: It will grow up and be able to work.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof of Steps 11–16 was rejected, רב אשי brings a new, successful proof for Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה forbids selling a fetus to a גוי, so our משנה follows him.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's stated reason for permitting a שבורה: it cannot be healed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה forbids a fetus, since it will be able to work. Our משנה can follow him.

steps.title: New question: selling an animal only for its fetuses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law is if someone sells an animal to a גוי only for its fetuses. It notes that the question applies according to both רבי יהודה and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: if someone sold an animal to a גוי only for its fetuses, what is the law? The question can be asked according to רבי יהודה, and it can be asked according to the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about a new case: selling only the rights to an animal's babies, not the animal itself. It also announces that it will now explain why this question applies according to both sides of the earlier מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we discussed selling a whole animal, or a broken one, to a גוי. In the new case the Jew keeps the mother animal and the גוי only gets her future offspring. The phrase תיבעי לרבי יהודה, תיבעי לרבנן tells us this is not just a question for one side. Both opinions face real doubt here.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them (opens a real open question)
For its fetuses, meaning only the rights to its future babies
Let it be asked; the question applies

steps.confusionAlert: The Jew did NOT sell the mother animal. He still owns her. The גוי only bought the rights to her babies.

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
If he sold an animal for its fetuses, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He keeps the mother and sells only the rights to her offspring.

phrases.english: The question can be asked according to רבי יהודה,
and it can be asked according to the רבנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the רבי יהודה / רבנן dispute about selling a שבורה and applies it to a new case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is it permitted to sell a גוי only the fetuses of a large animal, according to each side of the dispute?

steps.title: For רבי יהודה: maybe he forbids, because people may confuse it
steps.stepSummary: Side one for רבי יהודה: he permits only a broken animal, which nobody would confuse with a healthy one. A healthy animal sold for its fetuses could be confused with a full sale, so he would forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here is why it is a question for רבי יהודה. Maybe רבי יהודה permits only a broken animal, because people will not confuse it with a regular one. But a whole, healthy animal could be confused, so he forbids it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first possible way רבי יהודה might rule: forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A broken animal looks obviously different, so no one will think healthy animals may also be sold. Here the animal is healthy. People who see a deal made on it might think selling a whole healthy animal is fine. Because of that risk of confusion, רבי יהודה might forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: He only permitted up to here (his leniency is limited to this case)
To be confused or mixed up with something else

phrases.english: The question can be asked according to רבי יהודה:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָא שָׁרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: רבי יהודה only permitted
in the case of a broken animal,
since people will not come to confuse it,
phrases.notes: A broken animal looks clearly different from a healthy one.

phrases.english: but a whole animal, which people may confuse, he forbids.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא קָא שָׁרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first side of the doubt for רבי יהודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רבי יהודה's leniency limited to a case where confusion is impossible?

steps.title: For רבי יהודה: or maybe he permits, by a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: Side two for רבי יהודה: if he permits selling a broken animal, which leaves the Jew's ownership completely, then he should certainly permit this case, where the animal stays with the Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps: if a broken animal, which is completely separated from the Jew, is permitted, then a whole animal, which is not separated from him, should certainly be permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the opposite possibility for רבי יהודה: permitted, using a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the focus is ownership, not appearance. With a broken animal the Jew gives away the entire animal, yet רבי יהודה still permits it. With fetuses only, the Jew keeps the animal, so this is an even milder case and should surely be permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a doubt)
Cut off from him, fully out of his ownership

phrases.english: Or perhaps,
if a broken animal, which is fully separated from him, is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן שְׁלֵמָה דְּלָא פְּסַקָה מִינֵּיהּ?
phrases.english: then all the more so a whole animal, which is not separated from him!
phrases.notes: He keeps the mother animal and sells only her offspring.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא, וּמָה שְׁבוּרָה דִּפְסַקָה מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side of the doubt for רבי יהודה, set against Step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי יהודה's leniency apply even more strongly when the Jew keeps the animal?

steps.title: For the רבנן: maybe they permit, since the animal stays with the Jew
steps.stepSummary: Side one for the רבנן: they forbid a broken animal only because it fully leaves the Jew's ownership. Here the animal stays with him, so they might permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here is why it is a question for the רבנן. Maybe the רבנן forbid only a broken animal, because it is fully separated from the Jew. But a whole animal that is not separated from him, they permit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the question applies to the רבנן, starting with the side that says it is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן forbid even a broken animal. That might be because the whole animal leaves the Jew's hands. When he sells only the fetuses, the mother stays his, so the reason for their strictness is missing and they might permit it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion against רבי יהודה

phrases.english: The question can be asked according to the רבנן:
the רבנן only forbade
a broken animal, since it is fully separated from him,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שְׁלֵמָה דְּלָא פְּסַקָה מִינֵּיהּ — שָׁרוּ.
phrases.english: but a whole animal, which is not separated from him, they permit.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָסְרִי רַבָּנַן אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the two sides for רבי יהודה to the first side for the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the רבנן's strictness based only on the animal fully leaving the Jew's ownership?
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the same new case can turn into a possible leniency for the strict opinion and a possible strictness for the lenient opinion. Everything depends on the reason behind each view: confusion or loss of ownership.

steps.title: Side two for the רבנן: forbidden all the more so
steps.stepSummary: The other side for the רבנן: they forbid even a שבורה, which nobody would confuse with a healthy animal. So they would surely forbid a healthy animal sold for its fetuses, which could be confused.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe: if even a broken animal, which people will not confuse with a healthy one, is forbidden by the רבנן, then all the more so a healthy animal, which people will confuse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second side of its question for the רבנן. Maybe they would forbid this case even more strongly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 said the רבנן might permit this case because the animal stays with the Jew. This side flips it: the רבנן forbid a שבורה even though there is little risk of confusion. A healthy animal sold for its fetuses carries real risk of confusion, so it should be forbidden through a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)
To be confused or mixed up

phrases.english: Or perhaps:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה שְׁבוּרָה דְּלָא אָתְיָא לְאִיחַלּוֹפֵי — אָסְרִי,
phrases.english: If a broken animal, which people will not come to confuse, they forbid,
then all the more so a healthy animal
phrases.notes: Here a healthy animal sold only for its fetuses.

phrases.english: which people will come to confuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side to Step 21 for the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Would the רבנן forbid selling a healthy animal for its fetuses through a קל וחומר from a שבורה?

steps.title: Is confusion really the רבנן's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that the רבנן's reason is confusion. A ברייתא shows them telling רבי יהודה that a broken animal can still be bred and give birth, which sounds like their concern is the fetuses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really the reason of the רבנן? But a ברייתא teaches: They said to רבי יהודה, 'But people breed it and it gives birth!' So their reason seems to be its fetuses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to attack an assumption it used in the question. It had assumed the רבנן's reason was fear of confusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 assumed the רבנן forbid a שבורה because of confusion (Step 21 pointed instead to the animal leaving the Jew's ownership). The ברייתא suggests their reason is the offspring that would be born to the גוי. If that were true, a sale only for the fetuses would clearly be forbidden, and the whole question for the רבנן would fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא (introduces a challenge from a source)

phrases.english: And is the reason of the Rabbis because of this?
phrases.notes: "This" means the fear of confusion.

phrases.english: But it is taught: They said to Rabbi Yehuda:
But don't they breed it, and it gives birth!
Apparently it is because of its fetuses.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטַעְמָא דְרַבָּנַן מִשּׁוּם הָכִי הוּא? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind Steps 21-22 about the reason of the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the רבנן forbid a שבורה because of confusion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא quotes the רבנן pointing to breeding and birth, which suggests their reason is the fetuses and not confusion.

steps.title: The רבנן were arguing with רבי יהודה's reasoning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the רבנן's own reason really is confusion. In the ברייתא they were turning to רבי יהודה's reason: he treats a broken animal like one sold for slaughter, because it can never heal.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what they meant to tell him: Our reason is that people will confuse it with a regular animal. But you, why do you permit it? Because it cannot heal, so you treat it like an animal sold for slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer. The ברייתא does not show the רבנן's own reason; it shows them arguing against רבי יהודה's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן hold their own reason: a sale of a broken animal could be confused with a sale of a healthy one. Their words in the ברייתא were aimed at רבי יהודה. He says a broken animal that can never heal is like an animal sold for slaughter, and selling for slaughter is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what they were saying to him (reinterprets a statement)

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'don't they breed it and it gives birth' are not the רבנן's own reason for forbidding. They are an attack on רבי יהודה's reason. The רבנן's own reason stays confusion.

phrases.english: This is what they were saying to him:
Our reason is because people will come
to confuse it with a regular animal,
but you, what is your reason for permitting?
Because it cannot be healed,
so it is like one who sold it for slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 23 by reinterpreting the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the ברייתא's statement as an argument against the other side's reasoning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that the רבנן forbid because of the fetuses.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן forbid because of confusion. Their words in the ברייתא attack רבי יהודה's comparison to an animal sold for slaughter.

steps.title: The breeding argument: the gentile will keep the animal
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן finish their attack on רבי יהודה. A broken animal is not like one sold for slaughter, because it can still be bred and give birth. So the גוי will keep it alive for a long time instead of slaughtering it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But don't they breed it and it gives birth? And since they breed it and it gives birth, he will keep it around for a long time!
steps.whatsHappening: This completes the answer. It shows how the breeding line in the ברייתא works against רבי יהודה's comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said a broken animal is like one sold for slaughter. The רבנן reply that the גוי will not slaughter it soon, because he can breed it and get offspring. Since the גוי keeps it alive, it looks like an ordinary sale of a large animal, which is forbidden. The point about the fetuses was only meant to break the slaughter comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: He delays, keeps it for a while

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן forbid selling a שבורה because of confusion. Their breeding argument only shows that רבי יהודה's comparison fails: a broken animal is not like one sold for slaughter, because the גוי will keep it alive to breed it. So the question about selling for fetuses according to the רבנן still stands.

phrases.english: But don't they breed it, and it gives birth?
And since they breed it and it gives birth,
he will keep it for a long time!
phrases.notes: So it is not like an animal sold for slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer of Step 24 by explaining the רבנן's rebuttal of רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Completes the reinterpretation by showing that the breeding argument targets the slaughter comparison.
steps.terutzMaskana: Breeding means the גוי delays slaughter, so רבי יהודה's comparison to selling for slaughter fails. The רבנן's own reason stays confusion.

steps.title: רבי יהודה answers: a broken animal will not mate anyway
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה replies to the רבנן that he will worry about the animal giving birth when it actually happens. A broken animal does not accept a male, so this is not a real concern.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה said to them: 'When it gives birth, then we will talk, because such an animal does not accept a male.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the argument. רבי יהודה answers the רבנן's claim that a broken animal can still be bred and give birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן said the גוי will keep the broken animal alive because it can still have offspring. רבי יהודה says this almost never happens, because a broken animal will not let a male mate with it. So in his view it really is like an animal sold for slaughter. This ברייתא was only about רבי יהודה's reason, so it cannot tell us what the רבנן hold about selling an animal for its fetuses.

keyTerms.meaning: When it gives birth (then we can deal with it)
Accepts a male, meaning allows mating

steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the side-track. The ברייתא gives no proof about the רבנן's view on selling for fetuses, so the גמרא has to look for a new source.

phrases.english: And he (רבי יהודה) said to them:
When it gives birth (then I will worry about it),
phrases.notes: A dismissive reply: the scenario is unlikely.

phrases.english: since it does not accept a male.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהודה's rebuttal to the רבנן's argument in Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual rejection: the scenario raised against him does not really happen.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A broken animal can be bred, so the גוי will keep it alive.
steps.terutzMaskana: A broken animal will not mate, so it is effectively headed for slaughter.

steps.title: Proof attempt: the משנה does not call קבלנות forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove from our משנה that קבלנות with a גוי is allowed. The משנה adds 'although he is not permitted' only about selling, not about קבלנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: the משנה says 'and one who gives it to him in קבלנות,' and it does not add 'although he is not permitted'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to resolve the question from step 18 using our משנה. It suggests that giving an animal to a גוי in קבלנות, which is the same as selling it for its fetuses, is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קבלנות is very similar to selling the animal for its fetuses, because the גוי gets a share in the offspring. The משנה says 'although he is not permitted' only about selling. Since it does not say this about קבלנות, the proof suggests that קבלנות is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, which introduces a proof
Receivership: giving an animal to someone to raise in exchange for a share of the offspring
And it does not teach (the משנה left something out)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
and one who gives (an animal) to him (a גוי) in receivership,
and it does not teach:
"although he is not permitted"!
phrases.notes: In the משנה this phrase appears only by the case of selling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא fails to settle the question, the גמרא turns to the wording of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: Giving an animal to a גוי in קבלנות (and similar arrangements involving the offspring) is permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה, which says 'although he is not permitted' only about selling and not about קבלנות.

steps.title: Rejection: partnership is also left out, yet it is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The משנה also does not say 'not permitted' about partnership, yet אבוה דשמואל forbids partnership with a גוי because of a possible oath by עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your logic, partnership is also listed without 'not permitted.' Is partnership allowed too? But אבוה דשמואל said it is forbidden to partner with a גוי. Perhaps the גוי will owe an oath and swear by his idol, and the תורה said 'it shall not be heard from your mouth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof by pointing to another case in the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If leaving out 'not permitted' meant something is allowed, then partnership would also be allowed. But partnership is clearly forbidden, because the גוי partner might have to swear to the Jew and would swear by his idol. That falls under the prohibition of 'לֹא יִשָּׁמַע עַל פִּיךָ'. So the missing phrase proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning, which turns the other side's logic against them
"It shall not be heard from your mouth," a verse forbidding mention of idols

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not that the Jew himself swears by an idol. The worry is that the Jew causes the גוי to swear by his idol, and the verse forbids causing this too.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
one who enters a partnership with him, where (the משנה) also does not teach (this),
so too, is he permitted?
But Shmuel's father said:

phrases.aramaic: אָסוּר לְאָדָם שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה שׁוּתָּפוּת עִם הַגּוֹי,
phrases.english: It is forbidden for a person to make a partnership with a גוי,
lest he (the גוי) become obligated to take an oath to him

phrases.aramaic: וְנִשְׁבָּע לוֹ בְּשֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁלּוֹ,
phrases.english: and he will swear to him in the name of his idol,
and the תורה said:
"It shall not be heard from your mouth"! (Exodus 23:13)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in Step 27.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole method of learning 'permitted' from the משנה's silence.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same reasoning would permit partnership, which אבוה דשמואל clearly forbids.

steps.title: The משנה said it once, and it applies to all the cases
steps.stepSummary: The משנה wrote 'not permitted' only by selling, but the same applies to partnership and to קבלנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה taught selling, and the same is true for partnership. So too, it taught selling, and the same is true for קבלנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the rejection. The phrase 'not permitted' written by selling also covers the other cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since partnership must be forbidden even without the phrase, the phrase by selling must stand for the whole list. The same logic applies to קבלנות. So the proof from Step 27 fails, and קבלנות with a גוי is also not permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא (author of the משנה) taught

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's 'although he is not permitted' is written once by selling, but it applies to partnership and קבלנות too. All of these are forbidden with a גוי, even though the animal is exempt from בכורה.

phrases.english: Rather, (the תנא) taught selling,
and the same is true for partnership.
So too, he taught selling
and the same is true for receivership.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, תְּנָא מְכִירָה, וְהוּא הַדִּין לְשׁוּתָּפוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the rejection in Step 28 and applies it to קבלנות.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The phrase 'not permitted' by selling covers partnership and קבלנות too, so the proof that קבלנות is allowed fails.

steps.title: Why did the משנה pick selling?
steps.stepSummary: If the rule applies to all the cases, why did the משנה write 'not permitted' specifically by selling?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is special about selling, that the משנה chose it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a quick follow-up about the wording of the משנה. This sets up the short answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we say the phrase covers every case, it is fair to ask why it was attached to selling in particular. The question is only about the משנה's style, not about the law.

phrases.english: And what is different about selling, that he cited it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up question about the wording assumed in Step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה attached 'not permitted' to selling and not to the other cases.

steps.title: Selling is the main case
steps.stepSummary: The משנה mentioned selling because selling is the primary form of this prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because selling is the main (prohibition).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the wording question. Selling is the central case, so the משנה placed the phrase there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling hands the animal over completely, so it is the clearest and most basic case of the prohibition. The משנה wrote the phrase by the main case and expects us to apply it to the others.

phrases.english: Because the main (prohibition) is selling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Selling is the primary case of the prohibition, so the משנה wrote the phrase there.

steps.title: Come and hear: רבי יהודה on a Jew who receives an animal from a גוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new proof from a ברייתא. It begins with רבי יהודה's first case: a Jew who takes in a גוי's animal to raise for a share.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יהודה says, if someone takes in an animal from a גוי to raise and it gives birth, they estimate the firstborn's value, and he gives half its value to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא introduces a ברייתא to try again to answer the question from step 18 about selling an animal for its fetuses, which is like קבלנות. This first case is setup: the key proof line comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the Jew is the one receiving the animal from the גוי, so the Jew and the גוי each own part of it. רבי יהודה holds that the Jew's half is holy as a בכור. So he must pay half the animal's value to the כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the formula that introduces a source brought as a proof
One who receives an animal to raise in exchange for a share of it
They estimate it at its market value

phrases.english: Come and hear:
phrases.notes: Signals a proof is coming.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says,
one who receives an animal from a gentile
phrases.notes: The Jew takes the גוי's animal to raise for a share.

phrases.english: and it gave birth (to a firstborn) —
they assess it at its value,
and he gives half of its value to the priest.
phrases.notes: Only the Jew's half is treated as a בכור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the משנה failed, the גמרא turns to a ברייתא as a new source.
steps.raayaObject: Whether selling an animal to a גוי only for its fetuses is forbidden

steps.title: Giving an animal to a גוי in קבלנות is 'not permitted' and carries a fine
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's second case explicitly calls giving an animal to a גוי 'בקבלה' forbidden. חז"ל fine the person up to ten times the value.
steps.simpleTranslation: And someone who gives his animal to a גוי to raise, even though he is not allowed to, is fined up to ten times its value, and he gives its entire value to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the heart of the proof. The ברייתא openly says that giving an animal to a גוי in קבלה is 'not permitted.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the Jew owns the animal and gives it to the גוי. That is close to selling an animal for its fetuses, since the גוי gets a share of the offspring. The words 'אף על פי שאינו רשאי' suggest such an arrangement is forbidden. The fine is that he must buy back the גוי's share, even at a high price, and give the whole value to the כהן. The גמרא's evaluation of this proof comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: One who gives his animal to someone else to raise in exchange for a share
Even though he is not permitted
They fine (penalize) him, a rabbinic penalty
Up to ten times its value

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. In step 32 the Jew RECEIVES the animal from the גוי (הַמְקַבֵּל). Here the Jew GIVES his animal to the גוי (הַנּוֹתֵן). Only the giving case is called 'not permitted' and fined.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the line the proof depends on. In step 27 the משנה said 'not permitted' only about selling. Here a ברייתא says it directly about קבלה, which resembles selling for the fetuses.

phrases.english: And one who gives (an animal to a gentile) in receivership,
even though he is not permitted —
phrases.notes: The key words of the proof.

phrases.english: they penalize him up to ten times its value,
phrases.notes: He must buy out the גוי's share, even at a high price.

phrases.english: and he gives all of its value to the priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַנּוֹתֵן בְּקַבָּלָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and gives its decisive line.
steps.raayaObject: קבלנות with a גוי is forbidden, so selling an animal for its fetuses (the question of step 18) would also be forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה in the ברייתא: 'והנותן בקבלה אף על פי שאינו רשאי'

steps.title: חכמים: any ownership share of a גוי exempts the animal from בכורה
steps.stepSummary: חכמים disagree with רבי יהודה. As long as a גוי has any share in the animal, its firstborn is not a בכור at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: as long as the גוי has a hand in it, it is exempt from the law of the firstborn.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with the opposing view of חכמים about the בכורה law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה made the Jew pay for his share, and in the giving case the whole value. חכמים hold that any partial ownership by a גוי removes the בכורה status completely. So according to חכמים, nothing is owed to the כהן in either case.

keyTerms.meaning: The גוי has a share (a 'hand') in the animal
Exempt from the law of the firstborn
And the Sages say: introduces the opposing majority view

steps.whatToRemember: In this ברייתא, רבי יהודה says giving an animal to a גוי in קבלה is 'not permitted' and he fines the giver. חכמים say any share of a גוי exempts the animal from בכורה entirely.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
as long as the hand of the gentile is involved —
phrases.notes: Any partial ownership, in the mother or in the fetus.

phrases.english: it is exempt from the firstborn status.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁיַּד הַגּוֹי בָּאֶמְצַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא with the disagreeing view of חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any ownership share of a גוי in the animal exempts it from בכורה.
